[[Category:Production]]
The '''cost price''' of a product is the total cost to manufacture one unit of it.

It varies by production method and over time, according to raw material/energy/labour cost, as well as external/internal incidents affecting productivity.

== Calculation ==

$$
\text{cost price}
=
\frac{\text{total production cost}}{\text{number of functional units made*}}.
$$

<blockquote>
<nowiki/>*:[[Reject]]s must be excluded as they are not commercialisable products.
</blockquote>
